findings.description: The remediated generation head schema and RPC contract store the full (phase, transition_sequence) tuple in work_queue_projection_heads, enforcing exact head matching on submit, rejecting same-sequence/different-phase submissions without manufacturing second active generations, and restricting head movement strictly to reconciliation.

Both /work/submit and /work/reconcile explicitly define RFC 7807 409 Problem responses in the OpenAPI contract for projection conflict states (stale_projection, projection_generation_mismatch, reconciliation_required), ensuring transport-level specification completeness.

The final integration package (wp-integration) and coordinator package (wp-coordinator-queue) explicitly execute test_mcp_work_projection.py as part of their verification gates, ensuring transport parity for direct MCP projections is validated in end-to-end integration.

Reconciliation endpoint authorization maps to the existing submit_work policy action with mode=reconcile context, preserving security policy boundaries while enforcing strict RFC 7807 401/403 problem responses on authorization failure.

The autopilot state machine maintains a strict persist-first outbox ordering where loop-state write succeeds prior to queue projection, and resume reconciliation reconstructs queue projections strictly from loaded loop-state without treating queue state as authoritative.

The work-package DAG and write_allow scopes cleanly isolate contracts (wp-contracts), coordinator persistence (wp-coordinator-queue), bridge outbox seams (wp-bridge-projection), and cross-boundary integration validation (wp-integration) without scope overlap or circular dependencies.
